attempts.entry_title: Context-dependent sensorimotor transformation and retrosplenial cortex (Bech, Dard et al., eLife)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's behavioural findings held up in this data, and its optogenetic maps could not be tested. Licking to the whisker stimulus, the first-trial switch at context changes, and the modelled behaviour all reproduced, as did most of the widefield and photoactivation-control findings, though the expert-session count did not (318 sessions in 49 mice against 201 in 41) because the paper's set is a fixed list. The seven optogenetic map claims are blocked because the methods give a different shuffle null in different places and no threshold for an affected site. The retrosplenial context-discrimination ranking is also blocked, because the paper states two baselines that give different results, and the retrosplenial tracing is untestable because the images are not in the dataset. The Figure 4 trajectory finding did not reproduce, and the Figure 4 connectivity claims were never run.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Bech, Dard et al. on dandiset 001847, which holds the behaviour, orofacial tracking, optogenetic grid inactivation, muscimol and widefield calcium imaging sessions of the paper. It tests the behavioural context modulation and its time course, the optogenetic and pharmacological inactivation maps, the widefield dynamics on grid ROI traces, and the effects of inhibition on cortical activity and its low-dimensional trajectories. Mouse lines and session groups come from the session lists of the paper's processing code, as the files do not record them.

outcomes.notes: Of the 1497 sessions named by the 19 lists, 1467 (98.0%) are in the dandiset under the same identifier. Every session of every list a claim selects from is present with a readable trial table, and those lists' counts agree with the claims file (expert 41 mice and 201 sessions, opto 7 and 56, control 4 and 39, Context Off 7 and 21, jRGECO1a 6 and 25, GCaMP6f 8 and 33, tdTomato 4 and 15, GFP 6 and 24, wf-opto 4 and 40, photoactivation 2 and 6, model 21 and 60). The pool list sessions_Context_sessions, used for the expert rule's pool variant, does not match in full. It has 1451 entries for the stated 1449; 30 are written with a processing-date suffix (for example PB165_20231115_144956_2023_12_01) and are not dandiset identifiers, although all 30 sessions are in the dandiset under the plain identifier and none is also listed plainly; and 3 of its sessions (PB185_20240801_095038, PB186_20240801_110359, PB189_20240902_155436) have no readable trial table. So 1418 of the 1451 entries match with a trial table, which is partially reproduced under the criterion (at least 90%). The session types in the files agree with each list's purpose.

outcomes.notes: The Methods' rule (lower bound of the 95% bootstrap interval of the mean block contrast above 0.375), applied to the 1434 behavioural sessions described whisker_context, selects 318 sessions in 49 mice with 24.7 blocks per session, outside 201 ± 20.1 and 41 ± 4.1 (blocks within 23 ± 2.3). The tested sessions are of every type (888 behaviour-only, 364 widefield, 80 wf-opto, 74 opto, 28 pharmacology). Variants, the rule also run on the 60 sessions described context_... findings.statement: The files do not record the mouse lines. The subject genotype is "WT" for every mouse but one ("Ai148"), and strain is C57BL/6 for all, so no file says which mice carry VGAT-ChR2, jRGECO1a, GCaMP6f, tdTomato or GFP, or which received no opsin. The optogenetic, control and widefield groups can only be formed from the session lists of the paper's code.

Session groups are not recorded in a usable form. Muscimol and Ringer days, the injected area, baseline and injection days, and Context Off days have no field; the pharmacology, surgery and virus fields are "na" in every file, and most muscimol and Ringer sessions are typed behaviour_only_session. The Context Off trials still name pink and brown noise in context_background.

The DeepLabCut series (processing/behavior/BehavioralTimeSeries) carry the unit "seconds" and a conversion of 1/28 (side camera) or 1/24 (top camera) for every series, likelihoods and angles included. The positions are in pixels, the whisker_angle series is in degrees (it reproduces the paper's 97.3 and 98.6 degrees unconverted), and pupil_area is in square pixels, for which the conversion would have to be 1/28 squared.

No trial table column has a description (all "None"), and the perf codes 0 to 6 are not explained in the files; they were read from their cross-tabulation with trial type and lick (6 is an early lick).

lick_time minus the stimulus time is about 100 ms longer than the paper's spout-contact times (470 against 370 ms for auditory W+), while the context differences and the tests match; lick_time minus response_window_start_time, which is 100 ms after the stimulus, gives the paper's 370, 400, 392 and 418 ms. What lick_time is measured from is not described.

Three files (PB185_20240801_095038, PB186_20240801_110359, PB189_20240902_155436) have no BehavioralEpochs. In 76 of the 97 face-video sessions the DLC timestamps and data differ in length (printed in the DLC data cell), mostly by a few frames; in PB192_20241121_122848 the jaw series has 311,339 data points for 1,116,888 timestamps, and in PB177_20240529_121819 953,445 (jaw) and 948,779 (whisker) for 955,705.

The Methods' expert rule (block contrasts significantly above 0.375) applied to the dandiset selects 318 sessions in 49 mice; the paper's 201 sessions in 41 mice are the code's fixed list, which includes 12 sessions the rule rejects. How the list was chosen is not stated.

Question for the authors on Figure 2C-F. The Methods build the opto-map null by shuffling block labels; the legends and the code shuffle all trials. The block-label shuffle keeps the laser effect inside the null, and under it no named site reaches d' 0.8 (at most 0.57); the trial shuffle gives the published map. Which null was used, and at what d' is a site counted as affected (the colour scale starts at 0.5)? Seven claims are blocked on this.

Question for the authors on Figure 3C. Which trials are pooled for the jaw-opening onset of 108 ± 24 ms? The correct whisker trials of Figure 3B (W+ hits and W- misses) give 90 ms, W+ whisker hits 76 ms, the code's auditory and whisker hits 77 ms; the attempt assumed the Figure 3B set.
The light-sheet images of RSC axons (Figure 3, figure supplement 1C) are not in the dandiset and no other deposit is named.

Question for the authors on Figure 3H. Which pre-stimulus baseline is subtracted before the d' maps? The paper gives two, the 250 ms of the Methods' Computation of ΔF/F0 for Figures 3 and 4 and the 50 ms of the Methods for Figures 3E&F, whose d' Figure 3H uses; the code uses 100 ms. With 50 or 100 ms RSC is first in the pixel and ROI versions; with 250 ms it ties with wM1 in the pixel version, so the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

In 46 of the 46 widefield-with-optogenetics and photoactivation sessions, 910 of the trials (833 wf-opto, 77 photoactivation) have their first imaging frame after the stimulus more than one frame late, up to 81 s, so the imaging has gaps that the trial table does not mark.

entries.title: Context-dependent sensorimotor transformation and retrosplenial cortex (Bech, Dard et al., eLife)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Bech, Dard et al. on dandiset 001847, which holds the behaviour, orofacial tracking, optogenetic grid inactivation, muscimol and widefield calcium imaging sessions of the paper. It tests the behavioural context modulation and its time course, the optogenetic and pharmacological inactivation maps, the widefield dynamics on grid ROI traces, and the effects of inhibition on cortical activity and its low-dimensional trajectories. Mouse lines and session groups come from the session lists of the paper's processing code, as the files do not record them.
